_note: One plain-English line per box hadith card, printed on the card's back under the label 'In our words'. These are Noor Post's own words, NOT a translation: the saying itself is quoted exactly on the front from the fixed edition, per sourcing-rules.md. Written 2026-10-09 for a reader of about ten. DRAFT: each line must be checked by the scholar against the Arabic before print — a gloss that drifts from the meaning is worse than none. Envelopes with no saying selected (06, 10) have no gloss.

glosses.01: Being too mean even to say hello is the worst kind of stingy.
glosses.02: People who ask for advice before they decide end up doing the right thing.
glosses.03: If there is no kindness in you, you are missing every good thing.
glosses.04: A foolish person says whatever they feel. A wise person thinks before they speak.
glosses.05: Nothing goes together better than being gentle and knowing a lot.
glosses.07: What you are worth is the thing you do really well.
glosses.08: A good neighbour does not just avoid causing trouble. A good neighbour puts up with the trouble the neighbours cause.
glosses.09: Your tongue is too good for rude words.
glosses.11: This world is like a market: some people come out ahead, and some lose.
glosses.12: Be kind to people, and they will trust you to settle their arguments.
glosses.13: Being quiet is a door to being wise. It makes friends, and it leads to every good thing.
glosses.14: Showing something off before it is ready spoils it.
